# API contracts — the live, FastAPI-generated `/openapi.json` IS the contract

**Standard: every system API publishes an OpenAPI 3.1 spec, generated by FastAPI
from real Pydantic models + real routes.** No hand-authored `.yaml` file lives
in this directory anymore (mock-fx's `fx.openapi.yaml` and QMS's
`qms.openapi.yaml` both did, both were deleted): a parallel hand-written file
duplicating what the live app already generates is a drift risk with no
compensating benefit, not a second source of truth worth keeping. See git
history for those two files if you want the pre-migration framing.

## One shared action vocabulary, in the code itself

Each operation is bound to a domain action via `openapi_extra` on the route
decorator (not YAML) — see `src/mock-fx/mock_fx/api.py` or
`src/mock-qms/mock_qms/api.py` for real examples. `x-domain-action` /
`x-resource-type` / `x-authz-context` tie the HTTP surface to the
authorization model, the same triple the MCP tools and Cedar policies use;
`x-gap` marks a genuinely unresolved design question (still unimplemented,
stated plainly rather than guessed at) directly on the operation it concerns.

Example (real, from `mock_fx/api.py`):

```python
@app.get(
    "/exchange-rates/{base}/{quote}", response_model=ExchangeRate,
    openapi_extra={
        "x-domain-action": "fx-rate.read",       # -> business/decisions.md D1
        "x-resource-type": "ExchangeRate",        # -> authz-projection.yaml
        "x-authz-context": ["fx_age_seconds", "quote_currency"],
    },
)
def get_exchange_rate(base: str, quote: str, effectiveAt: str | None = None) -> ExchangeRate:
    ...
```

## Documenting a cross-service dependency: `x-consults`

OpenAPI has no native construct for "this endpoint calls another API
internally" (it describes the exposed HTTP interface, not server-side
implementation; the 3.1 `links` object is for client-side response->request
chaining, not this). ADR-010 (masterdata must be consumed via API, never a
duplicated file) is exactly this kind of dependency. Use `x-consults` in the
same `openapi_extra` dict -- a list, since an operation can depend on more
than one other service:

```python
openapi_extra={
    "x-consults": [{
        "service": "masterdata", "endpoint": "GET /currencies/{code}",
        "purpose": "validate base/quote are known currencies (ADR-010, fail closed)",
    }],
}
```

Same spirit as `x-domain-action` etc: makes a real, load-bearing dependency
machine-readable and diffable instead of only living in a docstring someone
has to already know to go read.

## Field-level `x-owner` / `x-role`

For schemas assembled from multiple systems' data (QMS's `QuoteVersion` is
the canonical example), per-field ownership is expressed the same way, via
`pydantic.Field(json_schema_extra={"x-owner": ..., "x-role": "owns"|"computes"|"references"})`
-- see `mock_qms/models.py`. Catches accidental duplication (two fields
independently claiming to own the same fact) before implementation, not after.

## Per system

| System | Spec | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CRM · TMS · Rate · QMS · Workflow | live `/openapi.json`, generated by FastAPI | no committed static file -- the running app IS the contract |
| FX | live `/openapi.json` | plain REST, APIKEY, no MCP |
